paper_metadata.title: Towards Pricing Financial Derivatives with an IBM Quantum Computer

summary: The paper implements a quantum principal component analysis (qPCA) prototype on the 5‑qubit IBMQX2 processor to estimate dominant eigenvectors of interest‑rate covariance matrices. A 2×2 matrix experiment used 3 qubits with 8192 shots per iteration and converged after ~4 iterations, while a 4×4 expansion (3 qubits total) required ≥18 entangling gates and produced unusable results on hardware due to noise. The work is a proof‑of‑principle NISQ demonstration for financial covariance analysis rather than a performance benchmark.

experiments.description: Hybrid qPCA experiment to estimate the dominant eigenvector/eigenvalue of a 2x2 cross-correlation matrix for two forward-rate maturities using IBMQX2 and Qiskit, with iterative eigenvector refinement and quantum phase estimation.

algorithm.variant: quantum principal component analysis (qPCA) with iterative eigenvector refinement and quantum phase estimation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterate until estimated eigenvector coefficients stabilize; paper reports stopping after 4 iterations for the 2x2 case
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start from random/heuristic initial state |b0> = (|0>+|1>)/sqrt(2); use the previous iteration's estimated eigenvector as the next initial state

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 2x2 covariance/cross-correlation matrix normalized by trace and encoded into a 1-qubit eigenvector register plus 2 qubits for 2-bit eigenvalue estimation
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the largest eigenvalue and corresponding eigenvector of the normalized covariance matrix rho2 = sigma2 / tr(sigma2)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection/projection onto the binary subspace corresponding to the largest eigenvalue estimate (|11>)

problem_instance.description: Historical interest-rate forward-rate cross-correlation matrix for two maturities

dataset_specification.description: Based on historical data for two time-maturing forward rates; 2x2 submatrix of the 3x3 covariance matrix from Wilmott (Ref. 33)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Normalize covariance matrix by its trace to form a density matrix; use historical cross-correlation data
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 4 iterative runs, each averaged over 8192 realizations; compare estimated coefficients across iterations and measure in multiple bases to infer relative phases

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise / decoherence / gate and measurement errors
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: basis averaging over x, y, and arbitrary r measurements; iterative refinement to reduce coherent errors

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct normalized covariance matrix from historical data
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert measured bitstrings to eigenvector coefficients; average over measurement bases; estimate fidelity/error bars from IBM-provided qubit and measurement fidelity plus statistical error

speedup_claims.caveats: Paper presents a NISQ proof-of-principle and does not report a classical baseline or empirical speedup.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated; experiment only demonstrated on a 2x2 covariance matrix.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require large-scale qPCA on high-dimensional covariance matrices with efficient state preparation and fault-tolerant phase estimation.
limiting_factors: State preparation assumptions for qPCA not demonstrated
Hardware noise and limited qubit count

notes: 3 qubits are explicitly described for the 2x2 case: 2 qubits for eigenvalue estimation and 1 qubit for the eigenvector.
The paper reports 8192 realizations per iteration.
No explicit circuit depth or transpiled depth is given for this sub-experiment.
No asymptotic speedup order is characterized; the paper presents a NISQ proof-of-principle.
Authors present the work as a proof-of-principle NISQ demonstration and do not claim experimental quantum advantage.
Problem instance is trivially solvable classically (2x2 matrix eigen-decomposition).

experiments.description: Quantum phase estimation refinement of the 2x2 qPCA experiment to estimate the dominant eigenvalue using the previously estimated eigenvector on IBMQX2 and Qiskit.

algorithm.variant: quantum phase estimation (QPE) used after qPCA eigenvector estimation
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initialize the eigenvector register with the estimated dominant eigenvector from the first stage

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the largest eigenvalue lambda_max of rho2 with 3-bit precision
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Phase-estimation projection onto the eigenvalue subspace

problem_instance.description: Same 2x2 normalized covariance matrix from the qPCA experiment

dataset_specification.description: Historical forward-rate covariance matrix, 2x2 submatrix of sigma3

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Use the estimated eigenvector from the first stage as the input state for QPE
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare simulator and real-chip output distributions; report fidelity of simulator-estimated eigenvector against the earlier estimate

experiments.description: Hybrid qPCA experiment on a 4x4 expansion of the same covariance matrix, estimating the dominant eigenvector/eigenvalue with a 2-qubit eigenvector register and 1 qubit for eigenvalue estimation on IBMQX2 and Qiskit.

algorithm.variant: quantum principal component analysis (qPCA) on 4x4 matrix with iterative eigenvector refinement
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterate until eigenvector coefficients stabilize; paper reports 4 iterations
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start from uniform superposition over the 2-qubit eigenvector register; use previous iteration output as next input

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 4x4 matrix encoded into a 2-qubit eigenvector register plus 1 qubit for eigenvalue estimation
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the largest eigenvalue and corresponding eigenvector of rho4
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Projection onto the dominant eigenvalue subspace

problem_instance.description: 4x4 expansion of the historical forward-rate covariance matrix

dataset_specification.description: 4x4 matrix derived from the same historical interest-rate data source as the 3x3 matrix

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Normalize by trace to form rho4; use the 4x4 expansion of the covariance matrix
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 4 iterations with 8192 realizations per iteration; compare chip and simulator coefficient estimates; measure in multiple bases to infer phases

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: basis averaging over x, y, and arbitrary r measurements

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Normalize covariance matrix and prepare uniform superposition initial state
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average measurements across bases to estimate relative phases; interpret the final measured state as the dominant eigenvector approximation

speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states the hardware result is meaningless due to >100% estimated error; no classical baseline or speedup claim is given.

limiting_factors: Circuit depth too high for NISQ hardware
